question: As per Census 2011, what was the percentage of scheduled tribes of the total population in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.086**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per Census 2011, the percentage of Scheduled Tribes (ST) in India’s total population was **8.6%**.
 
• The total Scheduled Tribe population in India was approximately **10.45 crore** out of the total population of 121 crore.
 
• Scheduled Tribes are officially recognized indigenous communities in India, identified under Article 342 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• Madhya Pradesh has the largest population of Scheduled Tribes in India, followed by Maharashtra and Odisha.
 
• Among the states, Lakshadweep has the highest proportion of Scheduled Tribe population at 94.8%.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Definition of Scheduled Tribes:** Scheduled Tribes are socio-economically disadvantaged indigenous groups that have been granted constitutional recognition and protection under Article 342 of the Constitution of India.
 
• **Reservation Policy:** Scheduled Tribes benefit from reservation in education, employment, and political representation to promote their development and inclusion.
 
• **Tribal Sub-Plan (TSP):** TSP is a strategy adopted by the Indian government to allocate funds and resources specifically for the socio-economic development of tribal communities.
 
• **Geographical Distribution:** Scheduled Tribes are primarily concentrated in central, northeastern, and southern regions of India, including states like Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and Jharkhand.
 
• **Notable Tribes:** Some of the prominent Scheduled Tribes in India include the Gond, Bhil, Santhal, Oraon, and Khasi tribes.
